item.title: Back to back atmospheric rivers forecast to bring heavy rain and mountain snow to California
item.description: Heavy rain and snow are forecast across California and Sierra Nevada through January 4, 2026. The first wave will target southern California with subtropical moisture, followed by a stronger system forecast to bring heavy rain and snowfall across central and northern regions of the state. Source

item.title: Long-duration M7.1 solar flare erupts from AR 4324, producing Earth-directed CME
item.description: A long-duration solar flare measuring M7.1 at its peak erupted from Active Region 4324 at 13:51 UTC on December 31, 2025. The event started at 13:12 and ended at 14:11 UTC. Source

item.title: Strong M6.0 earthquake hits near the east coast of Honshu, Japan
item.description: A strong and shallow earthquake registered by the USGS as M6.0 hit near the east coast of Honshu, Japan at 14:26 UTC on December 31, 2025. The agency is reporting a depth of 19.3 km (12 miles). EMSC is reporting M6.0 at a depth of 19 km (11.8 miles). Source

item.title: Alberta clipper reinforces lake-effect snow as heavy rain targets southern California into the New Year
item.description: A surge of Arctic air, reinforced lake-effect snowfall, and an atmospheric river are forecast to affect large portions of the United States from December 31, 2025, into January 2, 2026. Heavy snow is expected downwind of the Great Lakes and across parts of the Northeast, while southern California faces a flash flood risk as an atmospheric river moves onshore around New Year’s Day. Source

item.title: Shallow M6.0 earthquake hits southeast Indian Ridge
item.description: A shallow earthquake registered by the USGS as M6.0 struck the southeast Indian Ridge at 01:53 UTC on January 1, 2026. The agency is reporting a depth of 10 km (6.2 miles). EMSC is reporting the same magnitude and depth. Source

item.title: Record snow sinks multiple vessels at Juneau Harbor, triggers avalanche risk in Alaska
item.description: Record December snowfall reaching over 200 cm (80 inches) in Juneau, Alaska, caused multiple vessels to sink in the city’s harbors as heavy, wet snow accumulated. The heavy snow was driven by multiple atmospheric rivers, which brought heavy precipitation to much of the region through late December 2025. Source

item.title: Strong M6.5 earthquake hits Guerrero, Mexico
item.description: A strong earthquake registered by the USGS as M6.5 struck Guerrero, Mexico, at 13:58 UTC (07:58 LT) on January 2, 2026. The agency is reporting a depth of 35 km (21.7 miles). EMSC is reporting the same magnitude and depth. The USGS issued a Yellow alert for shaking-related fatalities and a Green alert for economic losses. Source

item.title: Polar Vortex disruption expected after January stratospheric warming
item.description: A Sudden Stratospheric Warming (SSW) event evolving over the Arctic through mid-January 2026 is forecast to weaken and displace the Polar Vortex, according to ECMWF and NOAA extended-range guidance. The disturbance is expected to propagate downward over the following weeks, raising the probability of Arctic air outbreaks and colder-than-normal conditions in parts of North America and Europe during the second half of January 2026. Source

item.title: Flash floods kill 17 and destroy 1 800 homes across Afghanistan
item.description: Flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall and snowmelt have killed at least 17 people and left 11 injured across Afghanistan since January 1, 2026. Over 1 800 homes and structures were destroyed in Herat, Badghis, and Faryab provinces, with authorities warning of continuing risk as moderate rainfall persists in western regions. Source

item.title: One dead after avalanche near Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia
item.description: One snowmobiler was killed by an avalanche on the Rockies Mountains in British Columbia on December 30, 2025. Source
